title: Encryption
description: New files are encrypted with the key you choose. Files already in the bucket stay as they are.
newFilesOnly: Only new files are encrypted. Files already uploaded stay as they are until you run “Encrypt existing”.
localHint: Files are encrypted with the key set when the server was installed. Use this when Vault is not in use.
vaultHint: The key stays in Vault. This server asks Vault to lock and unlock the key of each new file.
vaultHintOff: Connect Vault first under Settings → Vault (KMS).
kmsUnavailable: Vault is unavailable: new files cannot be saved to this bucket right now. Buckets without encryption still work.
publicKms: Public access to files encrypted with a Vault key is not possible. Make the bucket private first.
keyIdHint: Leave empty to use {{allowlist}} style name created for this bucket. Allowed pattern: {{allowlist}}.
readOnly: You can view these settings. Changing them needs a bucket administrator.
serverKeyMissing: Set STORAGE_SSE_MASTER_KEY and restart the server to turn on the server key.
upgradeBody: A live 1.5.0 follower on this Postgres database is not detected when it is missing from the cluster node list. That node cannot read a DSSE object. S3 PutBucketEncryption does not ask for this confirmation and does not see that follower either. A 1.5.0 leader runs 1.5.0 code and accepts PutBucketEncryption itself, so upgrading the leader last is not enough.
disableBody: New files will be stored without encryption. Files that are already encrypted stay encrypted and can still be read.
rotateBody: New files will be encrypted with the new key version. Existing files stay readable. To move them to the new version, run “Encrypt existing objects”.
encryptExistingHint: Files without encryption are encrypted. Files on an older key version move to the current version. The file bytes of an already encrypted file are not read. Encrypting a file that was stored without encryption replaces its ETag with the checksum of the encrypted bytes.
destroyBody: Every file in this bucket will be unreadable forever. They cannot be restored, even by an administrator.
destroyBackup: Destroying a server key deletes wrapped data keys from the current metadata only. An older backup of that metadata still contains them.
vaultDeleteFailed: Vault did not delete the transit key. The files in this bucket are still unreadable.
destroyNameHint: Type {{bucket}} to confirm. This cannot be undone.
destroyMismatch: The name does not match this bucket.
